issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s challenge to the landlord’s ownership does not amount to a disclaimer warranting eviction when it is a bona fide demand for proof of ownership and the tenant does not clearly renounce the tenancy or assert a hostile title.
material_facts: The tenant admitted that the plaintiffs were landlords, had paid rent to them, and had pursued standard-rent proceedings naming them as landlords.
The tenant questioned how ownership had devolved to the plaintiffs, but did not claim ownership for himself or assert that a third party owned the premises.
The plaintiffs sought eviction in part on a ground that required them to establish ownership, and the tenant’s challenge was directed to that requirement.
The lower appellate courts treated the tenant’s pleading as a ground for eviction based on conduct affecting the landlord’s interests.
issues.conclusion: The tenant’s pleading was not a clear and unequivocal denial of the landlord’s title or disclaimer of the tenancy and did not justify eviction on that ground.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 12(1)(c) of the M.P. Accommodation Control Act, 1961, denial of title or disclaimer can constitute conduct likely to affect the landlord’s interests adversely and substantially, but it must clearly and unequivocally renounce the tenant’s character as tenant by claiming title in the tenant or a third party. Sections 116 of the Evidence Act and 111(g) of the Transfer of Property Act inform that standard. A bona fide demand that a landlord prove ownership relevant to the eviction claim is not, without more, a disclaimer. The Court relied on Raja Mohammad Amir Ahmad Khan v. Municipal Board of Sitapur, Tej Bhan Madan v. II Additional District Judge, Majati Subbarao v. P.V.K. Krishna Rao, Kundan Mal v. Gurudutta, and Hatimullah v. Mahamad Abju Choudhury.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_case and tenant_admitted_landlordship and ownership_proof_was_relevant_to_eviction_claim and tenant_challenged_ownership_to_seek_proof and tenant_did_not_claim_hostile_title and tenant_did_not_clearly_renounce_tenancy

predicates.rent_control_eviction_case: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking a tenant’s eviction under rent-control law.
predicates.tenant_admitted_landlordship: The tenant acknowledged the claimant as landlord, including by paying rent or treating the claimant as landlord in related proceedings.
predicates.ownership_proof_was_relevant_to_eviction: The eviction ground relied on by the landlord required proof of ownership in addition to landlordship.
predicates.tenant_challenged_ownership_to_seek_proo: The tenant questioned the basis of the landlord’s ownership so that the landlord would prove it for the eviction claim.
predicates.tenant_did_not_claim_hostile_title: The tenant did not claim ownership for himself or assert that a third party held title to the premises.
predicates.tenant_did_not_clearly_renounce_tenancy: The tenant did not clearly and unequivocally disown his status as tenant.

issues.definition: When a tenant in a rent-control eviction proceeding accepts the landlord relationship and seeks proof of ownership relevant to the claim, without asserting hostile title or clearly renouncing the tenancy, the challenge does not make disclaimer-based eviction available.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant may be evicted when the accommodation is bona fide required for rebuilding and that work cannot be carried out while the tenant remains in possession.
material_facts: The trial court found that the premises were dilapidated and required reconstruction.
The trial court found that the landlord bona fide required the premises for reconstruction and that the work could not be carried out without vacant possession.
The finding on the rebuilding ground was not displaced in the appeals.
issues.conclusion: The tenant was liable to be evicted on the rebuilding ground, subject to compliance with the statutory procedure protecting the tenant’s opportunity to return to the accommodation.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12(1)(h) of the M.P. Accommodation Control Act, 1961 permits eviction where the landlord bona fide requires the accommodation for building or rebuilding and the work cannot be carried out without it being vacated. Section 18 governs the consequential protection and procedure concerning the tenant’s possible return to occupation.

predicates.rent_control_eviction_case: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking a tenant’s eviction under rent-control law.
predicates.landlord_bona_fide_rebuilding_need: The landlord genuinely required the accommodation for rebuilding.
predicates.rebuilding_cannot_be_done_with_tenant_in: The rebuilding work could not be carried out unless the accommodation was vacated.

issues.definition: If a landlord genuinely requires rebuilding and the work requires vacant possession, the tenant is evictable for that purpose, subject to the tenant’s statutory return protection.

issues.legal_issue: Before making an eviction decree for rebuilding, the court must follow the statutory procedure for determining whether the tenant elects to return to the accommodation after rebuilding.
material_facts: The tenant was held liable to eviction because rebuilding could not be carried out without vacant possession.
The Court directed the trial court to ascertain whether the tenant elected to return to occupation and to make the consequential orders required by the Act.
issues.conclusion: The eviction decree for rebuilding could proceed only after the trial court complied with Section 18, including ascertaining the tenant’s election concerning return to occupation.
issues.legal_principle: Section 18 of the M.P. Accommodation Control Act, 1961 requires the court, in a rebuilding eviction, to address the tenant’s election to be placed in occupation after the work and to make the consequential orders prescribed by that section.

predicates.rent_control_eviction_case: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking a tenant’s eviction under rent-control law.
predicates.rebuilding_eviction_ground_established: The accommodation was held to be bona fide required for rebuilding that could not be carried out with the tenant in possession.
predicates.tenant_may_elect_return_after_rebuilding: The applicable procedure gives the tenant an election concerning occupation of the accommodation after rebuilding.

issues.definition: When a rebuilding eviction is established and the tenant may elect to return, the court must determine that election before finalizing the eviction.
